newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 7.

text.p: Target cut to sweeten super scheme: A lowered savings target of about $120,000, along with a reinsurance plan safeguarding individuals against failed private pension funds, are key sweeteners in Treasurer Winston Peters's compulsory superannuation scheme to be unveiled today. Page 1.

Checks on imported cars to continue: The Customs Department would continue its crackdown on imported used cars despite new rules coming into force today that put the onus on used-vehicle importers to provide reliable documents for each car. Page 2.
South Island hydro lake levels falling: South Island hydro lake levels are falling quickly, with only half the average inflow into the lakes during the past week. Page 13.
Enerco sales boost expected: Gas company Enerco NZ will boost sales by more than $5 million in its current financial year as a result of increases in residential charges confirmed last week. Page 13.

Strathmore to distribute assets buyback: Listed investor Strathmore Group plans to distribute most of its assets to shareholders by way of a pro-rata buyback offer worth $17 million, or 45 cents a share. Page 14.
Telecom hits at user group: Telecom has dismissed calls for changes to the Commerce Act to curtail what its critics claim is its dominant position in the New Zealand market. Page 14.
Winebox waste of time, say business leaders: The winebox inquiry was a waste of time, money and Winston Peters' reputation, senior business leaders say.

Prof's plan interests dairy chiefs: The Dairy Board says it is prepared to look at a proposed change in the industry's structure put forward by University of Auckland marketing professor Wayne Cartwright.

Report hits out over dam failure: By-pass channels designed to divert flood water around the Opuha Dam were not in place when the earth dam collapsed on February 6, a Canterbury Regional Council report says.
NZ unfazed on exit plan from Cambodia: The New Zealand Government is staying cool on the fate of Kiwis living in Cambodia even as Australia moves to prepare an emergency evacuation plan.

Thistle faces competition: Plans for an extra 10,000 or so new hotel rooms in London by the turn of the century are continuing to put pressure on Brierley Investments' biggest asset, the Thistle Hotel group.
